messages:
Aisha: Quick sync on the 'prewarm bank' proposal. Idea: CP mints tenant-scoped prewarm_tokens; operator redeems tokens to spin prewarmed nodes in tenant pools. This isolates forecasting from node lifecycle.

Tom: Love it. Two concerns: token accounting correctness during operator restarts, and how we surface unused prewarm time for billing.

Riley: For restarts we should make claims transactional: operator calls Redeem(token_id) -> ClaimReceipt with lease_expiry and node_metadata. If operator dies, CP reclaims after lease_expiry.

Aisha: Agree. Lease_expiry must be slightly > expected prewarm time to cover startup jitter. Add a reclaim_grace window to avoid immediate double-spend.

Leah: Billing note: nodes spun via prewarm_tokens must carry labels: tenant_id, token_id, issuance_ts. Billing pipeline will aggregate idle_hours by token_id and tenant_id.

ops-bot: prewarm-bank-service v0.1 deployed to staging :white_check_mark:

Tom: Multi-region handling: CP should issue region-tagged tokens. Operator redeems tokens only for local region. If local tokens exhausted but global allowance exists, operator should consult locality policy (prefer latency, or prefer cost). We need a clear policy: default to local, fallback to cheapest-region up to X ms extra latency.

Riley: Implementation sketch:
```
service PrewarmBank {
  rpc IssueTokens(IssueRequest) returns (IssueResponse);
  rpc RedeemToken(RedeemRequest) returns (RedeemResponse);
  rpc RevokeToken(RevokeRequest) returns (RevokeResponse);
}
message RedeemResponse { string node_id = 1; int64 lease_expiry = 2; }
```

Riley: Redeem must be idempotent for token_id; include operator_id in the call so CP can detect orphaned leases.

Aisha: Rollout plan: 1) CP issue-mode: read-only issuance logs for 48h 2) operator redeem endpoint local canary with 2 small tenants 24h 3) enable billing labels in canary 4) compare predicted vs actual prewarm utilization.

Marco: Metrics to add: prewarm_tokens_issued, tokens_redeemed, token_reclaim_count, prewarm_node_idle_seconds, prewarm_cost_allocated.

Leah: Also add predictive_confidence gauge and token_issue_rate. If confidence drops below threshold, CP throttles issuance.

Tom: Edge case: double-issue when CP scales horizontally. Use strong leader election or consistent hashing for issuance responsibility. Simpler: central issuance service behind leader; more complex: sharded issuance with vector clocks. Start central.

Aisha: Good pragmatic choice. We'll start with leader-based issuance and revisit if we hit a bottleneck.

Riley: Security: operator must present mTLS creds and an aud claim containing operator_id when redeeming. Token ids should be unguessable UUIDs.

Aisha: Action items: A) Riley: proto and idempotency semantics B) Tom: billing label spec C) Marco: dashboard panels + SLOs D) Leah: region-fallback policy doc E) all: add canary checklist to RFC follow-up.

Marco: I'll own dashboards. Putting panels on staging console dashboard for canary.

Leah: I'll draft region-fallback policy and a short playbook for when tokens are overused in one region.

ops-bot: Canary pipeline triggered for prewarm-bank operator canary :rocket:

Aisha: Thanks team. Post updates into the RFC follow-up doc and ping when PRs are up. End thread.
